description: The hallucination trap (PRD FR35, Section 12). A seeded set of deliberately fabricated claims that the verifier must reject every time, plus one grounded claim it must accept. The fabricated claims are built against the bundled office_intrusion scenario at the default seed (1337), so each cites a real event id but asserts a fact the evidence does not support, or cites an event that does not exist, or cites a malformed id. The test asserts the hallucination-rejection rate is 1.0 on this set.

claim.text: On WIN-ACCT-07, CORP\jdoe ran an encoded PowerShell process spawned from Word.

fabricated.name: fabricated_event_missing_id
fabricated.description: A wholesale invention: ransomware that never happened, citing an event id that does not exist in the store.

claim.text: The attacker deployed ransomware that encrypted the file server.

fabricated.name: time_mismatch
fabricated.description: Cites the real PowerShell process-create event but moves it six hours earlier.

claim.text: Word spawned the encoded PowerShell at 02:42 UTC, hours before the alert.

fabricated.name: principal_mismatch
fabricated.description: Cites the real process-create event but attributes it to the domain administrator.

claim.text: The domain administrator spawned the encoded PowerShell from Word.

fabricated.name: action_mismatch
fabricated.description: Cites the interactive logon event but calls it a process creation.

claim.text: CORP\jdoe created a new process at the start of the session.

fabricated.name: object_mismatch
fabricated.description: Cites the real lateral-movement logon but points it at the wrong source host.

claim.text: CORP\svc-backup logged on to the file server from 10.9.9.9.

fabricated.name: malformed_citation
fabricated.description: Cites a record number instead of a real event id, so the citation is malformed and provides no support.

claim.text: An encoded PowerShell process was created from Word.
